questions.question: The opening verse of Surah Al-Hajj describes the zalzalah of the Hour as a cosmic event of tremendous magnitude that will affect all of humanity.
questions.explanation: Verse 1 describes the zalzalah (convulsion) of the Hour as 'shay'un azim' — a tremendous thing — using the universal address 'O mankind' to signal that this event encompasses all of humanity without exception.

questions.question: What vivid scene does verse 2 use to illustrate the overwhelming terror of the Day of Judgment?
options: Mountains crumbling into dust while seas dry up
People staggering as though drunk though they have not consumed anything
The sun rising from the west as stars fall from the sky
Angels descending in visible form to all of humanity simultaneously
questions.explanation: Verse 2 describes nursing mothers abandoning their infants, pregnant women losing their pregnancies, and people appearing intoxicated yet sober — 'wa ma hum bi-sukara' — conveying the complete psychological overwhelm of that Day.

questions.question: Which sequence of embryonic stages does verse 5 list as evidence for the reality of resurrection?
options: Nutfah, then alaqah, then mudghah, then birth as an infant
Alaqah, then nutfah, then mudghah, then bone
Mudghah, then alaqah, then dust, then bone
Nutfah, then mudghah, then alaqah, then spirit
questions.explanation: Verse 5 traces human development from dust (turab), then nutfah (sperm-drop), then alaqah (clinging clot), then mudghah (lump of flesh — both formed and unformed), then birth as an infant. The God who accomplished this journey can also restore life after death.

questions.question: The person described in verse 11 as worshipping Allah 'on an edge' is someone whose faith becomes stronger and more deeply rooted when hardship strikes.
questions.explanation: Verse 11 describes a person whose faith collapses under trial: if good comes they are content, but if fitna strikes he turns on his face, abandoning Islam — the Quran calls this the manifest loss of both worlds.

questions.question: When Allah commanded Ibrahim to proclaim Hajj to all people, verse 27 describes pilgrims responding by coming in what manner?
options: Only by sea and during the officially appointed months of the year
On foot and on lean camels from every distant mountain pass
In large organized groups led by appointed guides from every nation
Only during the sacred months by the permission of the ruling authority
questions.explanation: Verse 27 promises that pilgrims will come 'rijalan' (on foot) and on every lean camel, arriving from 'kulli fajjin amiq' — every deep mountain pass — in response to Ibrahim's proclamation, fulfilling Allah's promise across all generations.

questions.question: What reason does verse 39 explicitly state for granting the believers permission to fight?
options: To establish Islamic governance over all territories
To avenge the deaths of Muslims in Mecca
Because they were wronged
Because their enemies had broken a formal peace treaty
questions.explanation: Verse 39 states 'udhina li-alladhina yuqataluna bi-annahum zulimu' — permission is given to those who are fought because they were wronged. The justification is explicitly defensive and rooted in injustice suffered.

questions.question: The fly parable of verse 73 argues that all false gods combined could not create a single fly, and if a fly snatched something from them they would be powerless to retrieve it.
questions.explanation: Verse 73 states that if all those called upon besides Allah gathered together they could not create a fly, and that fly could snatch from them and they could not recover it — exposing both the inability to create and the inability to act, rendering worship of such entities irrational.

questions.question: Which hadith source did Ibn Kathir cite in his commentary on verse 5 to support the Quranic account of the stages of fetal development?
options: A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim narrated by Ibn Masud describing 40-day stages
A report attributed to Imam al-Shafi'i in his al-Umm describing the soul's arrival
A narration from Hasan al-Basri stating the stages were figurative descriptions
A medical treatise cited by Imam al-Tabari as conforming to Quranic language
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir cited the famous hadith recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim from Ibn Masud, in which the Prophet described the nutfah remaining forty days, then becoming an alaqah for forty days, then a mudghah — after which the angel breathes the soul into the fetus.

questions.question: Classical scholars including Imam al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir agree that verse 39 of Surah Al-Hajj is the first Quranic verse ever revealed granting permission for armed conflict.
questions.explanation: Imam al-Tabari records reports from Ibn Abbas, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Qatadah, and others affirming this. Ibn Kathir in Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim also confirms this position, noting the passive 'udhina' (permission was given) as indicating divine authorization at the highest level.

questions.question: In his commentary on verse 30, Ibn Kathir cited a hadith in which the Prophet paired false speech with which other major sin?
options: Murder and theft from an orphan
Associating partners with Allah
Breaking family ties and consuming usurious interest
Abandoning the prayer and withholding zakat
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir records a hadith from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim in which the Prophet declared the greatest sins include associating partners with Allah and disobeying parents, then added: 'And false speech and false testimony' — repeating it so insistently that the companions wished he would stop, illuminating verse 30's pairing of idol worship and false speech.

questions.question: According to a narration from Ibn Abbas preserved by Imam al-Tabari, in the fly parable of verse 73 the 'seeker' refers to the fly trying to escape from the idol.
questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas stated 'the seeker is the idol and the sought is the fly' — meaning the idol would be seeking to reclaim what the fly snatched, yet cannot. This is the dominant reading recorded by al-Tabari and preferred by Ibn Kathir as most consistent with the context.

questions.question: Imam al-Tabari in Jami al-Bayan records whose opinion that the earthquake of verse 1 refers to the tremor occurring at the actual onset of the Day of Judgment itself?
options: Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah
Ibn Abbas and Alqamah
Mujahid and Said ibn Jubayr
Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah
questions.explanation: Al-Tabari records the view of Ibn Abbas and Alqamah that the zalzalah is the actual tremor of the Day of Judgment's arrival. He also records the view of Qatadah that it is a sign occurring before the Hour is established, but the Ibn Abbas and Alqamah view is the one Ibn Kathir also follows.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran described Ibrahim's proclamation of Hajj in verse 27 as demonstrating which principle?
options: That Hajj was first practiced by the angels before being given to humanity
That a single divine command delivered through one man generated the greatest annual human gathering in recorded history
That Hajj attendance is only spiritually valid for those who travel by difficult means
That the call to pilgrimage was restricted to the Arabian peninsula until Islam's spread
questions.explanation: Sayyid Qutb noted in Fi Zilal al-Quran that this single command to a lone prophet in a barren valley has generated, across fourteen centuries, the greatest annual gathering of human beings in history — growing rather than diminishing with time as a testament to divine power.

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir described the inclusion of monasteries, churches, and synagogues alongside mosques in verse 40 as establishing which principle?
options: That all religions are equally valid paths to salvation according to Islam
That Islam's defensive mission is universal in its commitment to preserving conditions for the worship of the One God
That Muslim rulers must financially subsidize non-Muslim religious institutions
That Islamic jurisprudence treats all houses of worship as legally equivalent to the mosque
questions.explanation: Al-Zuhayli notes in Al-Tafsir al-Munir that the explicit inclusion of sawami' (monasteries), biya' (churches), and salawat (synagogues) alongside mosques demonstrates that Islam's defensive purpose is not sectarian but universal — protecting wherever Allah's name is abundantly mentioned.

questions.question: Muhammad al-Sha'rawi observed that verse 75 concludes with the divine names 'All-Hearing' and 'All-Seeing' to reassure believers that no sincere turning toward truth goes unnoticed by Allah.
questions.explanation: Muhammad al-Sha'rawi noted the beauty of closing a passage about false worship with the affirmation that Allah both hears and sees everything — no sincere effort to follow the prophetic path escapes divine awareness, and no act of rejecting His messengers goes unseen.

questions.question: According to Fakhr al-Din al-Razi in Mafatih al-Ghayb, the sha'air Allah (divine symbols) function only as a mirror reflecting the believer's existing inner piety outward.
questions.explanation: Al-Razi argued in Mafatih al-Ghayb that the sha'air function as two-way signs: they reflect the believer's inner state outwardly, but they also strengthen and deepen taqwa through regular performance — making them both an educational and devotional institution, not merely a passive reflection.

questions.question: Muhammad al-Sha'rawi described verse 11's warning about conditional, fair-weather faith as actually being a form of divine mercy. Why?
options: Because it promises worldly prosperity to those who remain firm through difficulty
Because it educates believers about the nature of true faith before they are tested so they can fortify themselves in advance
Because it assures that no trial will ever exceed what a believer can bear
Because it guarantees that trials are always a sign of special divine love
questions.explanation: Muhammad al-Sha'rawi observed that Allah is educating believers about the nature of true faith before it is tested, so they can fortify themselves in advance. The verse is thus a mercy: a warning delivered before the event rather than a rebuke delivered after failure.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran noted that the timing of the permission to fight granted in verse 39 teaches believers what lesson about Islam's approach to conflict?
options: That defensive warfare is the highest form of worship and must be prepared for at all times
That the Quran's approach is characterized by extreme reluctance and patience, with permission only coming after all other avenues were exhausted
That armed resistance should begin at the first sign of oppression without awaiting divine permission
That the permission was purely a political strategy to consolidate the Muslim state in Medina
questions.explanation: Sayyid Qutb writes in Fi Zilal al-Quran that the permission came after thirteen years of persecution in Mecca, demonstrating that Islam's approach to conflict is characterized by extreme reluctance and patience — permission arrived only when all other avenues had been exhausted.
